post.text:
🚨 ChatGPT traffic has fallen -22% in the last 6 weeks, since the Gemini 3 launch.

7-day avg visitors has gone from ~203M to ~158M. Might be the holiday slump, but Gemini, their biggest consumer competitor, has remained flat and is now ~40% of ChatGPT.

Source: SimilarWeb. https://t.co/lud3N6pRzK

comments.name: The Profit Pup
comments.text:
The numbers are eye-opening: a 22% drop in ChatGPT web traffic over just 6 weeks while Gemini holds steady at ~40% relative share feels like more than just a holiday slowdown.

Google's real advantage seems to be frictionless integration, Gemini is already living inside Search, Gmail, Docs, and Android for hundreds of millions of users. You don't have to decide to "go to the AI"; the AI comes to you.

Meanwhile, many power users (including some vocal ones in the replies) are citing rate limits, perceived quality regressions, or overzealous safety layers pushing them toward alternatives.

Still, web traffic only tells part of the story app usage, API calls, and embedded experiences aren't captured here, so the full picture might be more nuanced.

What’s your take? Is this the beginning of a real redistribution of daily AI habits, or do you think OpenAI bounces back strong in Q1? And for those switching: what finally tipped the scale for you? Curious to hear the community's real experiences. 🤔🚀
